rows.t: Schedule 2, Mowing and Edging; standards feed KPI-M in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The pitch and its grass surrounds are cut so that, at every event, the playing surface is at the height the sporting code and the event specify, uniform across its full extent, free of clippings and cut litter, undamaged by machinery, and presented to broadcast standard.
Between events the surface is maintained so that this condition can be reached for the next event in accordance with the events timetable and without stress or damage to the turf.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3); grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4); fixed and moveable assets within those zones. Hybrid or reinforced turf zones identified on the zone plan.
LoS 2 Pitch, training and non-event weeks.
LoS 4 Grass surrounds inside the perimeter.
True Cut Height within the code range at readiness sign-off. (Appendix 1 – code target cut height and tolerance range); Measured as True Cut Height, not mower setting.

Prism gauge or approved turf height gauge; 15-point grid plus 4 run-off points fixed on the zone plan (Appendix 2 – Mowing height grid sampling). Height log with grid readings, mean, range and photographed gauge readings.
Supplier after every cut; Principal’s Representative or independent assessor at readiness and at least twice monthly unannounced
No grid point outside the code cut height tolerance range. No visible banding, corrugation, scalping or stripe-height difference.
Same grid readings as M1.1; range calculated; photo standard for banding and corrugation in Schedule 3.
Height held within the code growing range at all times. No single cut removes more than one third of leaf (base specification target 20 to 30%).
Height log before and after each cut showing leaf removed; spot gauge checks at audits.
Supplier every cut; Principal’s Representative at audits
KPI-M monthly deduction if breached at audit
Straight stripe pattern sideline to sideline from the dead-ball or goal line in the pattern the code or broadcaster specifies. Final cut within 24 hours of kick-off.
Visual audit against the code pattern drawing and Schedule 3 photo standards; dated photographs from the stand.
No clippings, clumps or windrows on the playing surface. No cut material on hard surfaces, assets, or gardens. No loose litter mown.
LoS 1 to 4; every event and every cut
Visual audit, whole zone walk plus perimeter and asset check; photographs.
Supplier every cut; joint readiness walk; Principal’s Representative spot audits

Neat, true mechanical edge at every vertical asset and hard surface; grass at edges within the mowing height range; no band of taller grass at the mowing perimeter; no soil gap at hard edges. Chemical edging only by approval and <50 mm wide.
Visual audit against Schedule 3 photo standards; edge width measured where chemical edging is approved.
Joint readiness walk; Principal’s Representative spot audits
No wheel rutting, skid or turn marks, ribbing, scalping or divoting from mowing. No damage to assets or infrastructure.
Visual audit: Clegg hammer or equivalent where rutting or compaction is suspected; damage register; Supplier early-warning notice before any complaint.
Supplier every cut; Principal’s Representative at audits
KPI-M monthly deduction per confirmed incident
No disease, stress or thinning attributable to cut height, frequency or dull blades.
Agronomic condition audit at fixed monitoring plots (cover, density, disease, root depth, leaf tissue where needed); monthly report with trends.
Principal's agronomist monthly; Supplier weekly inspection
KPI-M monthly deduction if decline is mowing-attributable

blocks.t: Standards M1.1 to M1.8 feed KPI-M, Mowing and Presentation. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here. Cut counts do not enter KPI-M; they are reconciled annually against the declared band (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for mowing:
Equipment fleet and why it suits the surface e.g., reel capability for match preparation, rotary for recovery cuts, pedestrian equipment for areas ride-on cannot reach, turf tyres)
Blade and cylinder maintenance regime and how sharpness is verified
How height is set and checked on site
The seasonal mowing strategy for cool-season and warm-season growth, including use of growth regulators
Clipping management
Event-week sequence of cuts, pattern and final cut timing
Resourcing, cover for absence
Wet-weather and no-mow decision rules
Where practicable, all fields are mown when the grass is dry (after morning dew has dried, or later in the day after morning rain) to prevent bunched clippings
How edging is sequenced with mowing.
All mowing plant and equipment complies with health and safety law and the stadium site rules; operators are trained and inducted.
Agrichemical edging and growth regulators are used only with the Principal's written approval and under the stadium's environmental controls.
Moveable assets are moved by hand or approved means, never pushed by mowers, and replaced before leaving site.
Any asset or turf damage is reported to the Principal's Representative on the same day and repaired at the Supplier's cost.
Clippings and vegetative material leaving site go to an approved facility.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code, kick-off time, pattern and broadcast requirements 10 working days before commencement; gives uninterrupted pitch access in the agreed preparation windows; decides closures and non-sporting uses and bears the recovery consequences under Schedule 1; and attends the joint readiness sign-off. Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-M for that event is assessed against the revised window.
Priced as an annual lump sum per level of service with a declared minimum and maximum cut band (tender pricing schedule, Mowing and Edging). The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Schedule 2, Line Marking; standards feed KPI-L, Line Marking and Field Presentation, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

At every event the field is marked to the Laws of the Game of the code and competition being played, with lines that are dimensionally accurate, straight, uniform in width and colour, bright and clearly visible to players, match officials, broadcast and video review, and applied without damage to the turf. Only the lines of the code being played are visible at kick-off. Between events, lines are maintained or removed so the field can be presented for the next event and code in accordance with the events timetable and without stress or damage to the turf.

Field of play, in-goal and run-off zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3); technical areas, officials' and warm-up markings and optional off-field marks within the perimeter fence (Z4). Includes seasonal and event set-out, maintenance re-marking, code changeover (removal of superseded lines and full set-out of the new code), and fixed survey reference points for each code layout. Logo, sponsor and distance-numeral painting is included only where instructed for an event.

LoS 1 Event marking (match and broadcast events). LoS 2 Training and non-event layouts. LoS 3 Code changeover. LoS 4 Ancillary and perimeter markings (technical areas, warm-up zones, optional marks, instructed logos).

Field of play, in-goal and all markings set out to the Laws of the code and competition being played. Every check dimension within 50 mm of the code dimension; field diagonals equal within 100 mm. Only the lines the code specifies are marked.

Steel tape, laser or GNSS check of length, width, both diagonals and the code check dimensions (football: goal area, penalty area, penalty mark, centre circle; rugby union: 22 m, 10 m, 15 m and 5 m lines; rugby league: 10 m transverse lines, 20 m and 40 m lines). Dimension record against the code drawing filed at each set-out.
Supplier at each set-out and changeover; Principal’s Representative or match commissioner at readiness sign-off

All lines of a code the same width. Football and rugby union: target 100 mm (<120 mm); goal line equal to goal post width. Rugby league: to the competition plan; 40 m lines unbroken red, 150 mm. Tolerance 10 mm.
Rule measurement at 10 fixed check points per code on the zone plan (proposed); readings recorded with photographs.

Lines straight, true and continuous when viewed from either end; no more than 20 mm off a string line over any 20 m length. Arcs and circles true to radius; corners square. Rugby union dashes 5 m long at the Law 1 positions; rugby league broken-line marks no more than 2 m apart; transverse lines across the full width.
String-line offset check at fixed audit points; visual check from each end and from the main broadcast camera position; dated photographs.
Supplier after marking; joint readiness walk

Lines bright and uniform in colour: white, and red where the code requires (rugby league 40 m lines). No gaps, skips, feathered edges, overspray, drips, double lines or shadowing. Clearly visible to players, officials, broadcast and video review, including under floodlights.
Visual audit against Schedule 3 photo standards from pitch level and the broadcast gantry; floodlit check for evening events.
Joint readiness walk; Principal’s Representative spot audits
Event marking completed after the final cut (M1.4) on MD-1 or match day and ready for sign-off at least 4 hours before kick-off. Training and non-event layouts complete before the scheduled start.
Marking log with date and finish time, cross-checked against the mowing log and the readiness sign-off time.
Supplier every marking; Principal at sign-off

Superseded lines removed or masked with approved water-based green-out paint so they are not visible from the stands or on broadcast, and the new code marked to L1.1 to L1.4 within the agreed changeover window. No turf staining or damage from removal.
Visual audit from pitch level and the stands against Schedule 3 photo standards; changeover log; dimension record for the new code.
Joint readiness walk for the next event

Technical areas, optional 9.15 m marks, warm-up zones, officials' marks and any instructed logos or distance numerals placed to the code, competition and broadcast drawings within 100 mm. Logos never cross or obscure a playing line. Football technical area no more than 1 m either side of the seated area and up to 1 m from the touchline.
Tape check against the competition and branding drawings; photographs.

No wheel marks, rutting, scalping or turf damage from marking equipment; no paint spills or transfer; no scorch, yellowing or line burn attributable to paint, growth regulators or line removal; no herbicide used.
Visual audit; monthly agronomic condition audit at fixed plots including turf under lines; damage register; Supplier early-warning notice before any complaint.
Supplier every marking; Principal's agronomist monthly
KPI-L monthly deduction per confirmed incident

subs.title: Code marking schedule (referenced by L1.1 to L1.3)

rows.t: International field of play 100 to 110 m long by 64 to 75 m wide; stadium layout 105 m by 68 m. Goal area 5.5 m and penalty area 16.5 m from the inside of each goal post and into the field; penalty mark 11 m from the midpoint between the posts; centre circle and penalty arc radius 9.15 m; corner arcs radius 1 m; optional marks 9.15 m from the corner arc, off the field and at right angles to the goal and touch lines. Lines continuous, all the same width and not more than 120 mm; goal line width equal to goal post width (goals 7.32 m by 2.44 m). Technical areas marked. Only Law 1 lines are marked.

Field of play 94 to 100 m long by 68 to 70 m wide; in-goal 6 to 22 m deep. Solid lines: dead-ball, touch-in-goal, try, 22 m, halfway and touch lines. 5 m dashes: 5 m and 15 m from and parallel to each touchline, 10 m either side of halfway, and 5 m from each try line. 0.5 m centre mark across halfway. Where the field is shorter or narrower, the 10 m, 22 m and 15 m lines move in proportion. Lines the same width, not more than 120 mm, matching post width. Perimeter area 5 m where practicable. Flag post positions (14) marked where sockets are not fixed.

Field of play 100 m between goal lines by 68 m wide; in-goal 6 to 11 m. Transverse lines every 10 m across the full width, including halfway, 20 m and 40 m lines; each 40 m line one unbroken red line 150 mm wide. Broken lines 10 m and 20 m from and parallel to touch, with marks or dots no more than 2 m apart. Distance numerals, corner post positions and other markings to the competition plan. For adult games, dimensions as near the maximum as possible.

Only the lines of the code being played are visible at kick-off; different-colour multi-code marking (B1.1.11) is not used. Fixed survey reference points at the field corners and centre are set once and used for every code layout.

blocks.t: Standards L1.1 to L1.8 feed KPI-L, Line Marking and Field Presentation. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here. The number of re-marks does not enter KPI-L; full code set-outs and changeovers are reconciled annually against the declared band (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for line marking:
The equipment fleet and surface fit (e.g., GNSS or robotic set-out and marking, pedestrian sprayers, turf tyres, string lines)
The set-out method and the fixed survey reference points for each code, with coordinates recorded
The paint products, colours and dilution rates for each code and season, and how brightness is held for broadcast
The marking order (widthways lines first, then touchlines and lengthways lines) and string handling to avoid ghost lines
How marking is sequenced with mowing (final cut lengthways then widthways, then marking) and with irrigation and rolling
The event-week sequence and final marking time
The code changeover method, products and window
Line removal after events and line-burn management
Logo and branding application where instructed; resourcing, cover for absence, and wet-weather decision rules
Only turf-approved, water-based, non-toxic line marking paint is used.
Herbicides are never used for line marking unless approved in writing or directed by the Principal’s Representative.
Growth regulators or stickers are used only with the Principal's written approval, and any damage from incorrect rate or method is repaired at the Supplier's cost.
Line set-out is completed only by the Supplier; no team, club, competition or broadcaster marks the field unless approved in writing by the Principal's Representative.
Mistakes and spills are corrected with approved green-out paint before leaving the field.
Any delay or risk of non-completion is reported to the Principal's Representative immediately and no later than 4 hours before kick-off.
Paint is stored, mixed and washed out under the stadium's environmental controls with no washwater to stormwater.
All marking plant complies with health and safety law and the stadium site rules
Operators are trained and inducted
Any turf or asset damage is reported on the same day and repaired at the Supplier's cost.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code, competition, field dimensions, marking drawing, line colours, logos and broadcast requirements 10 working days before commencement; supplies competition and sponsor branding drawings and stencils where these are competition items; sets the code changeover windows in the calendar; arranges the match commissioner or referee pitch inspection; and attends the joint readiness sign-off.
Where the calendar, code or marking drawing changes inside the notice period, KPI-L for that event is assessed against the revised window.

Priced as an annual lump sum per level of service with a declared minimum and maximum number of full code set-outs and changeovers (the marking band); event re-marks are included in the lump sum. Instructed logos, sponsor branding, distance numerals and additional marking requested by a team or competition are priced from the Schedule of Rates and approved in advance by the Principal's Representative. The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Schedule 2, Irrigation Management; standards feed KPI-I, Irrigation and Water Management, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The pitch root zone is held within the moisture band that gives the playing surface the firmness, traction, growth and recovery the sporting code and event require, wetted uniformly to depth across its full extent, with no water stress, over-watering, disease or scorch attributable to irrigation, and using no more water than the turf needs. The irrigation system is kept leak-free, operating to its design performance and ready for every event.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4). Irrigation assets serving those zones: controllers and central control software, weather station and rain sensor, in-ground soil moisture sensors and handheld probes, pump station and headworks, backflow preventers, mainlines, laterals, valves, sprinklers, quick couplers, water meters, data loggers and telemetry, and any non-potable bore. Includes hand watering and syringing, minor repairs, and the annual inspection. Capital renewal and system redesign remain with the Principal. Includes operation, protection and data management of TAU's own irrigation monitoring and control system (in-ground soil moisture sensors, rain and weather data, flow metering and the monitoring platform). Any additional monitoring equipment is sourced by the Supplier and approved by the Principal before purchase.
LoS 1 Pitch, event weeks (Premier). LoS 2 Pitch, training, non-event, renovation and grow-in weeks. LoS 3 Run-off and warm-up zones. LoS 4 Grass surrounds and irrigation system assets.

subs.title: Performance standards and measurement (one row per standard)

rows.t: Volumetric water content at readiness sign-off within the event band for the code: 20-25 % at 40 mm depth. No grid point more than 5% from the sports field mean. No surface water or localized soft areas.
Approved moisture probe (e.g. POGO; TDR350) on the 15-point grid plus 4 run-off points used for M1.1; readings logged electronically with mean, range and map.
Supplier MD-1 and match day; Principal’s Representative or independent assessor at readiness sign-off

Moisture held within the band set for the root zone in the Turf Management Plan; base specification target 25-30% unless the agreed root zone band differs. No visible water stress, wilt or localised dry patch; no evidence of over-watering such as ponding, algae, soft surface or anaerobic layers.

Probe readings on the fixed grid at least twice weekly in the growing season (proposed) and in-ground sensor data; visual audit; moisture log with trend chart. In-ground soil sensor data from TAU's monitoring system used alongside probe readings; sensor and probe readings compared monthly.
Supplier weekly; Principal’s Representative at audits; Principal's agronomist monthly
KPI-I monthly deduction if breached at audit

Irrigation wets the root zone evenly to the full extent of the sand profile and returns it to field capacity without drainage loss. Lower-quarter distribution uniformity at least 0.75 at the annual catch-can audit and after any system change. Heads and valve boxes level and 25 mm below the turf surface.
Catch-can uniformity audit by zone, with results and remedial actions; soil cores or probe at depth after irrigation; head level check; photographs.
Supplier annual audit; Principal's agronomist monthly spot check
KPI-I monthly deduction if breached at audit

Watering windows managed in accordance with event calendar and weather conditions. No irrigation during rainfall, line marking drying time, bump-in, or while covers or overlays are in place. Pre-match or half-time watering only where the competition allows and the match commissioner agrees, applied uniformly to the whole pitch.
Controller and central control logs cross-checked against the event run sheet, rain sensor and weather station data. Rainfall and weather data from TAU's monitoring system used to suspend irrigation.
Supplier weekly log; Principal’s Representative at audits
KPI-I monthly deduction per confirmed incident
No disease outbreak, scorch or turf damage attributable to irrigation timing, ponding or leaf wetness duration.
Agronomic condition audit at fixed monitoring plots; disease records; leaf wetness and weather data where available.
Principal's agronomist monthly; Supplier weekly inspection
KPI-I monthly deduction if decline is irrigation-attributable

Damaged or poorly performing components isolated within 2 hours of discovery or notification and repaired within 4 hours of isolation; alternate watering in place if the repair window likely to cause turf stress or damage. In event weeks, any fault in Z1 to Z3 repaired before readiness sign-off. Replacement heads and nozzles matched to existing; reinstated turf flush with no subsidence.
Fault and repair register with times of discovery, isolation and repair; time and date verified photographs; post-repair inspection.
Supplier every fault; Principal’s Representative at audits
KPI-I monthly deduction per confirmed late repair

Water applied within the seasonal water budget in the Turf Management Plan, reported as L/m2 per zone. No leaks, continuous running or irrigation during rainfall. Any bore take within consented daily and annual limits. Actual use tracked against the water allowance set by TAU.

Water meter and telemetry data, controller run times and probe data reconciled monthly against the budget; leak alerts and Watercare notices logged. Flow data from TAU's monitoring system, and bore telemetry where present, reported to Schedule 1, Section 10.
Supplier monthly report; Principal’s Representative review

Annual inspection of the whole system completed in the agreed off-season window and the Condition Report (repairs, costs, timing, inefficiencies and improvements) submitted by 1 September or the agreed date. Sprinkler heads and valve boxes marked before renovation, physical treatment or events. Monitoring system sensors and sensor markers included in the annual inspection. Costed repair and renewal recommendations for the next financial year provided before 30 September for TAU's operating budget.
Irrigation Condition Assessment Form in the approved format; headworks and bore report; marking checked at the pre-event walk.
Supplier annually; Principal’s Representative review on receipt
KPI-I monthly deduction if late or incomplete
Irrigation monitoring system operation and data

TAU's irrigation monitoring and control system operated to TAU's guidance and the manufacturer's instructions, with soil moisture and rainfall thresholds and irrigation schedules set as agreed in the Turf Management Plan. Sensors online and reporting, with data available for at least 95% of the time each month; faults reported within 24 hours. Sensors, valve boxes and markers undamaged.
Monitoring system data availability and alert report; device fault log; threshold and schedule change log; sensor markers checked at the pre-event walk.
Supplier weekly platform check and monthly report; Principal's Representative review

Leaks, continuous running and irregular water use identified by monitoring system alerts, Watercare smart meter notices forwarded by TAU, or site inspection are responded to and logged through the Principal's request-for-service (RFS) process within the RFS timeframes: Critical, response 1 hour and completion 2 hours; Priority 2, response 4 hours and completion 8 hours; Urgent, response 24 hours and completion 48 hours. Where not resolved at the first visit, the site is made safe and water isolated.
RFS records with response and completion times; before and after photographs; leak register reconciled to monitoring system and meter data.
Supplier every alert; Principal's Representative monthly
KPI-I monthly deduction per late response

subs.title: Event irrigation schedule (referenced by I1.1 and I1.4)

rows.t: Root zone at the event band at kick-off. Pre-match and half-time watering only where the competition regulations allow it and the match commissioner agrees; applied uniformly across the whole pitch and completed within the agreed time before kick-off or the restart.
Players generally prefer a firm, dry surface: moisture at 40 mm depth of 20-25% at kick-off. No pre-match watering unless agreed with the match officials.
Firm, even surface at the event band (moisture 20-25% depth at 40 mm). Any pre-match watering only as agreed with the competition and both teams.
Root zone brought to the upper end of the root zone band before any covers go down; no irrigation while covers are in place; recovery irrigation after removal under the recovery plan.

subs.title: Irrigation monitoring and control systems (referenced by I1.2, I1.7, I1.9 and I1.10)

rows.t: Manage irrigation timing, zones and schedules (IRRINET, Rainbird, Hunter, Toro and others). The Supplier operates and programmes the controllers and keeps them secure and functional.

Smart meter with data logger: near real-time water-use data that identifies irregular consumption from leaks or improper irrigation. Watercare notifies TAU, who forward the issue to the Supplier for investigation (I1.10). Conventional meters give monthly use and are being replaced with smart meters.
Irrigation flow meter and pulse counter

Dedicated flow meter (one per field where required) or a pulse counter on a pulse-output water meter, accuracy within 3 percent, transmitting volume and flow rate to TAU's monitoring system for water efficiency analytics (I1.7).
Handheld probes (e.g. POGO, TDR350) used by the Supplier for the fixed grid readings (I1.1, I1.2).
Connected to the controllers to support scheduling and stop irrigation in rain. Rain data from TAU's monitoring system or a local gauge is used to stop irrigation in rain (I1.4).

TAU's own system for soil moisture, rainfall and water-use monitoring. The Supplier operates it to TAU's guidance, protects in-ground sensors and markers, checks the data weekly and reports faults within 24 hours (I1.9).
Water meter telemetry to Auckland Council's Hydrotel portal, with backup power and data storage; checked in the annual headworks inspection against consented daily and annual limits (I1.7, I1.8).
Any additional monitoring equipment is sourced by the Supplier, compatible with TAU's system, and approved by the Principal before purchase. The Supplier operates, protects and reports on the system.

blocks.t: Standards I1.1 to I1.10 feed KPI-I, Irrigation and Water Management. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here. Water volumes do not enter the event score; they are scored monthly against the seasonal budget under I1.7.

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for irrigation:
The root zone moisture band by season and the event band for each code, and how they were set
The soil moisture monitoring method and equipment, probe grid, in-ground sensor locations and calibration
How irrigation is scheduled from evapotranspiration, weather forecast, sensor and probe data, including the controller and central control settings
The seasonal water budget by zone in L/m2
Event-week and match-day watering, including pre-match and half-time watering where allowed
Wetting agent programme
Management under covers and during recovery, renovation and grow-in
Hand watering and syringing
Drought and water restriction plans
The annual inspection, uniformity audit and condition report
The fault response, spares holding and repair process; and the named Irrigation Specialist and cover for absence.
Monitoring system operation: soil moisture and rainfall thresholds and irrigation schedules, and how sensor, probe and weather data are combined in scheduling decisions
Monitoring data management: weekly system checks, alert response, tracking of water use against TAU's allowance, and the monthly water efficiency report
Protection of in-ground sensors, valve boxes and markers during mowing, aeration, renovation, goal post changeover and events
Training and competence of all relevant staff in the controllers, monitoring tools and TAU's monitoring system
The Supplier provides a suitably qualified Irrigation Specialist as a key person (any change requires the Principal's approval)
All irrigation work complies with health and safety law, the stadium site rules, the backflow and water supply requirements of Watercare, and any resource consent for bore water.
Specialist or more than minor repairs (e.g., pumps, electrical and control systems, significant excavation) are completed by an approved subcontractor.
Backfill is placed in consolidated layers no deeper than 200 mm with root zone matching the existing.
Issues with system operation, performance or water supply are reported to the Principal's Representative before turf damage occurs
Failure to give early warning may result in repairs at the Supplier's cost (B3.2, F2.1).
Water restrictions issued by Auckland Council or Watercare are followed.

TAU's irrigation monitoring system is operated to TAU's guidance and the manufacturer's instructions, and all relevant staff are trained, competent and proficient in the irrigation controllers and monitoring tools.
The Irrigation Specialist champions irrigation management using the monitoring and control systems, in line with the water efficiency objectives, KPIs and reporting requirements.
In-ground soil sensors stay installed in their valve boxes, concealed and marked; the Supplier does not disturb or relocate them, and repairs any damage it causes at its own cost.

Leak management response is completed through the Principal's request-for-service process in accordance with the KPIs, documentation and reporting; Watercare irregular-use notifications forwarded by TAU are investigated as a request for service.
Unlocked irrigation cabinets or controllers, system failures, design inefficiencies and water-stressed turf are reported through Eyes and Ears early warning.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code, kick-off time, cover or overlay dates and any pre-match or half-time watering request 10 working days before (proposed); provides access to the controllers, central control software, meter and telemetry data and the Hydrotel portal; holds the capital renewal programme and decides on system upgrades from the Condition Report; and attends the joint readiness sign-off.
Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-I for that event is assessed against the revised window.

The Principal provides access to its irrigation monitoring system and data; maintains, replaces and renews the system; sets the water allowance; and forwards Watercare irregular-use notifications to the Supplier.

Irrigation management, monitoring, the annual inspection and uniformity audit, and reporting are priced as an annual lump sum per level of service. Minor repairs <$1,000 are completed without prior approval and claimed with an itemised cost breakdown and photographs; repairs >$1,000 or needing a specialist subcontractor are quoted and approved by the Principal's Representative before work starts.
Water is supplied by the Principal.

Operation, protection, data management and reporting of TAU's irrigation monitoring system are included in the annual lump sum. Additional monitoring equipment sourced by the Supplier is priced from the Schedule of Rates and approved before purchase. Leak response follows the minor repair cost thresholds.

rows.t: Schedule 2, Goal Posts; standards feed KPI-G, Goal Posts and Equipment, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

At every event the goals or goal posts for the code being played are installed to the Laws of the Game, plumb, secure and safe, with padding and nets fitted to the competition's requirements, and presented clean and white to broadcast standard. Code changeovers are completed within the agreed window without damage to the turf, the sockets or the posts, and posts not in use are stored safely and kept in sound, inspected condition.

Football goals, nets and net supports; rugby union and rugby league goal posts, crossbars and padding; ground sleeves, sockets, caps, pins, wedges and securing fittings; goal post racks and storage areas; installation and removal plant. Includes event set-up and pack-down, weekly safety inspection, code changeover, socket and turf reinstatement, cleaning, painting and touch-up, storage, and the annual condition inspection. Renewal and replacement of posts and sleeves remain with the Principal.

LoS 1 Event set-up (padding, nets, final checks). LoS 2 Installed posts between events (weekly inspection, cleaning). LoS 3 Code changeover (removal, installation and socket reinstatement). LoS 4 Storage, painting and condition inspection.

Goals or posts installed to the code specification and requirement, centred on the goal or try line with the line marked to match. Width and crossbar height within 10 mm of the code dimension; uprights plumb within 10 mm over 3 m.
Tape or laser measurement of inside width and crossbar height at each post; spirit level or inclinometer on each upright; installation record with photographs.
Supplier at installation; Principal’s Representative or match commissioner at readiness sign-off

Posts fully seated and pinned or wedged in their sleeves with no movement; football goals anchored so they cannot tip; no sharp edges, protruding bolts or loose fittings. Nets complete, taut and secured so they do not interfere with the goalkeeper; net supports outside the field of play.
Pre-event check including a hand-load test of each upright and crossbar; photographs.
Supplier before every event; joint readiness walk

Rugby union and rugby league posts padded for every match and for training when instructed, with padding complete, clean, undamaged and secure. Rugby union: external edge no more than 0.5 m from the post. Rugby league: at least the bottom 2 m of each upright. Competition or sponsor padding fitted as supplied.
Visual check and tape measure of padding depth; padding register showing fitting, removal and storage; photographs.
Supplier before every event; joint readiness walk

Posts, goals and crossbars clean and uniformly white, with no tape, foreign objects, rust, chips or bare metal visible from the stands or on broadcast. Painted posts with at least two coats of exterior semi-gloss white acrylic to AS/NZS 2311; powder-coated posts touched up with colour-matched two-pot epoxy.
Visual audit against Schedule 3 photo standards from pitch level and the broadcast gantry; painting record with product data.
Joint readiness walk; Principal’s Representative spot audits

Removal and installation for a change of code completed within the agreed changeover window and before the new code is line marked (L1.6). Unused sockets capped flush, level and safe, and turf reinstated to match the surface, with no trip hazard.
Changeover log against the window; visual and straight-edge check of each capped socket; photographs.
Joint readiness walk for the next event

No turf damage, rutting or compaction from installation plant and equipment, and no damage to posts, sleeves, padding or nets during handling. Approved ground protection used where the surface is wet or soft. Any damage repaired to at least original condition at the Supplier's cost.

rows.t: Schedule 2, Nutrition Management; standards feed KPI-N, Nutrition and Turf Condition, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The sports fields are fed through a nitrogen-led programme, with nitrogen rate and carrier matched to turf growth potential and the event calendar, so that the turf is healthy, dense, actively growing and uniformly green, with the wear tolerance and recovery the calendar demands. For every event the turf peaks in colour, density and strength without a growth surge that softens the surface or adds clippings, and worn areas are fed to recover after the event. All other nutrients are held at or above the MLSN guideline by supplying only what the nitrogen-driven growth will use, and every product is applied evenly, at the planned rate, without scorch, volatilisation, run-off or leaching.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4). Includes soil and leaf tissue testing, the monthly nitrogen plan and carrier selection, the MLSN supply calculation for the other nutrients, the event peaking programme, recovery feeding after events, renovation and non-sporting use, product procurement, storage and records, equipment calibration, application and reporting. Wetting agents, growth regulators and pest and disease products sit in the Turf Treatment service area and are coordinated with this programme.

subs.title: Nitrogen carrier schedule guidelines (referenced by N1.2, N1.6 and N1.7)

rows.t: Release, strengths, cautions and role in the programme
Polymer or sulphur coated urea (controlled release)

Release over weeks, governed by temperature and moisture. Even, steady growth with low loss. Use mini or micro prill sized for fine turf so prills are not picked up by mowers or left on the surface. Role: base feeding in non-event and growing periods, applied at least 8 days before an event.
Released by soil microbes, so slow in cold soils and faster in warm. Low burn and leaching risk. Role: base feeding in warm periods.
Released by water rather than microbes, so it still works in cool soils. Role: base feeding in cool periods.
Fast, low cost per kg N. Volatilisation risk if left on the surface, so watered in or used with a urease inhibitor. Low-rate foliar use. Role: foliar peaking and recovery feeding.
Fast, works in cool conditions, supplies sulphur, acidifying. Track pH against the MLSN guideline of 5.5. Role: cool-weather response, peaking and recovery.
Fast nitrate nitrogen with potassium for wear tolerance; supplies K counted in the MLSN calculation. Role: pre-event and recovery feeding, cool weather.
Fast nitrate nitrogen effective at low temperature; supplies Ca counted in the MLSN calculation. Role: winter response and recovery.
Slow microbial release, warm soils only, low analysis. Role: limited, as part of base feeding where approved.

At least 50% of annual nitrogen from controlled or slow release carriers; the balance from soluble and foliar carriers for peaking, recovery and cool-weather response. Granular carriers stop 8 days before an event; foliar carriers are used inside that window.

subs.title: MLSN supply calculation guidelines (referenced by N1.1 and N1.3)

rows.t: Set the monthly nitrogen rate from turf growth potential (calculated from site air temperature for the turf species), adjusted for event load and recovery needs, up to the maximum monthly rate in the Turf Management Plan. The annual total is the nitrogen budget.
Estimate the use of each other nutrient from the nitrogen budget: K 0.5 x N; P 0.125 x N; Ca 0.125 x N; Mg 0.05 x N; S 0.05 x N.

Supply needed = (expected plant use + MLSN guideline) minus the soil test level, for each nutrient, worked over a root zone of 1 m2 to 150 mm depth (1 g/m2 equals about 4.4 mg/kg). If the soil test is already above the total, none is applied.
Count nutrients supplied by nitrogen carriers (K from potassium nitrate, S from ammonium sulphate, Ca from calcium nitrate) before adding any other product.
Re-run the calculation at each soil test and when the nitrogen plan changes by more than 10%.

subs.title: Event peaking programme (referenced by N1.6 and N1.7)

rows.t: Nutrition requirement (rates and products set in the Turf Management Plan; figures proposed)

Tier A: internationals, finals and marquee broadcast events. Tier B: regular season competition matches. The Principal confirms the tier of each event with the event calendar. Tier A events receive the full programme below, including pre-event tissue testing; Tier B events receive the 14-day to match-day steps.

Leaf tissue test and review against the sufficiency ranges. Correct any deficiency (K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn) through the MLSN calculation. Set the nitrogen plan to hold steady growth into the event, not a surge.

Last granular nitrogen, if any: controlled or slow release carrier, light rate, watered in. Potassium nitrate where wear tolerance is needed. No granular product after day 8 so no granules remain on the surface.

Foliar peaking application: low-rate soluble nitrogen (5 to 10 kg N/ha) from urea or ammonium sulphate, with iron (1 to 3 kg Fe/ha) and manganese as needed, for colour and density without a growth surge. Timed with the mowing plan (M1.1 to M1.4), irrigation (I1.1) and any growth regulator in the Turf Treatment service area.
No nitrogen, except an iron-only colour touch-up agreed with the stadium turf manager. No foliar application in the 24 hours before line marking, so paint adheres to dry leaf (L1.4).

Recovery nitrogen from soluble carriers (potassium nitrate, ammonium sulphate or calcium nitrate in cool weather) to worn areas or the whole pitch, combined with divot repair, seeding or renovation where planned. After non-sporting use or covers, feed to the recovery plan once covers are removed.
One combined recovery and peaking foliar application 2 to 4 days before the next event, at the lower end of the peaking rate.

Peaking rates and carriers are set separately for warm and cool growing periods. In cool conditions ammonium and nitrate carriers and iron are favoured for colour; in warm conditions nitrogen is kept low before events to avoid soft, lush growth.

rows.t: Minor sports turf repairs (divoting, plugging, turfing and seeding)
Schedule 2, Minor Sports Turf Repairs; standards feed KPI-R, Surface Repair and Recovery, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

Localised surface damage (divots, scars, wear, grass loss, holes and level changes) is repaired promptly so that at every event the playing surface is safe, level, stable underfoot and visually uniform, with repaired areas matching the surrounding turf in species, profile, colour and density and able to carry play. Damage is repaired before it becomes a larger reinstatement, a loss of use or an injury risk, without harm to the surrounding turf or assets.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4). Includes post-event damage inspection and divoting; plugging, turfing and seeding of localised damage; minor level correction by topdressing; repair of damage from goal post changeover, irrigation repairs and minor vandalism; donor and harvest area management and reinstatement; establishment irrigation and grow-in monitoring. Repairs beyond the minor repair threshold, and full-field renovation, are instructed separately.

LoS 1 Pitch, event weeks (post-event divoting and repairs before the next event). LoS 2 Pitch, training, non-event and grow-in weeks. LoS 3 Run-off and warm-up zones. LoS 4 Grass surrounds, donor and harvest areas.

Turf healthy, dense, free of weeds, pests, disease and thatch, matching the existing species and profile (sand-based turf on sand fields), at least 50 mm thick in high-wear areas. Supplier monthly; Principal's Representative at audits
