No damage to surrounding turf, irrigation heads, in-ground moisture sensors, goal post sockets or line markings from repair work; spoil, off-cuts and debris removed off-site to an approved facility.
Visual audit; damage register; Supplier early-warning notice before any complaint.
Supplier every repair; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-R monthly deduction per confirmed incident

subs.title: Repair method selection (referenced by R1.2 to R1.6)

rows.t: After every event, across the whole field of play. Divots replaced root-down and firmed, or filled with divot mix of matching sand and seed; surface brushed and level before the next mow.
Small, localised damage such as holes, stud scars and small bare patches. Plugs cut with an approved plugger from a matching donor area, at least 50 mm deep (100 mm in high-traffic areas), set flush.

Preferred repair for anything larger than plugging, and for any repair needed in an event week or in high-wear zones (goalmouths, penalty spots, scrum and ruck zones, centre). Sand-based turf matching the root zone, at least 50 mm thick in high-wear areas.

Only where there is enough time to establish before use (generally 4 to 6 weeks), as an emergency treatment, or across extensive thin areas. At least two directions; establishment irrigation for at least 14 days.
Minor depressions up to 10 mm corrected by sand topdressing matched to the root zone; deeper depressions lifted, re-levelled and relaid.
Turf repairs completed at least 5 days before kick-off so they root; plugging up to MD-2; divoting straight after each event; no seeding in event week other than divot mix.

Repairs above the minor repair threshold (25 m2 in one area or 100 m2 across the pitch after one event), or recurring failure in the same area, are reported to the Principal's Representative and instructed as renovation.

blocks.t: Standards R1.1 to R1.10 feed KPI-R, Surface Repair and Recovery. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here.
Repair quantities do not enter KPI-R; turf, seed and divot mix used are reconciled annually against the declared repair band (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for minor sports turf repairs:
The post-event inspection and damage mapping method, and how all staff report damage
The divoting plant and equipment and method, crew size and timing after each event, and the divot mix specification
Repair method selection and the excavation depths for each method
Turf source and specification (grower, species, root zone, thickness), and any on-site nursery or donor area
Seed species, rates and establishment programme
Event-week repair timing and how repairs are sequenced with mowing, line marking, irrigation and nutrition
Establishment irrigation and grow-in monitoring
Protection of irrigation heads, in-ground moisture sensors and goal post sockets during repairs
Escalation to renovation when damage exceeds the minor repair threshold
Resourcing and cover for absence
Turfing is the preferred repair; seeding is used only where the conditions in R1.6 are met.
Turf and seed match the existing sports field species and root zone profile; sand-based turf only on sand fields.
Pre-plant fertiliser and wetting agent are used as approved in the nutrition programme.
Spoil, turf off-cuts, roots, stones and debris are removed off-site to an approved facility.
Repairs that fail to establish, or damage caused by the Supplier, are made good at the Supplier's cost.
Any surface hazard is made safe the same day and reported to the Principal's Representative.
All plant and equipment complies with health and safety law and the stadium site rules; operators are trained and inducted.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code and kick-off time 10 working days before commencement; gives access for post-event divoting and repairs straight after each event; approves the turf source and any on-site nursery or harvest area; decides on escalation to renovation; bears the recovery cost of damage from non-sporting use under Schedule 1; and attends the joint readiness sign-off.
Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-R for that event is assessed against what could be repaired in the revised window.

Post-event inspection, divoting and minor repairs are priced as an annual lump sum per level of service, with a declared minimum and maximum annual repair band (m2 of turf, kg of seed and tonnes of divot mix). Repairs beyond the band, or above the minor repair threshold, are priced from the Schedule of Rates and approved in advance by the Principal's Representative.
The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Sports turf maintenance treatments (pest, disease, earthworm and weed control; growth regulators; wetting agents)
Schedule 2, Sports Turf Maintenance Treatments; standards feed KPI-T, Turf Health and Treatments, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The pitch and its surrounds are kept free of damaging pests, disease, earthworm casting and weeds, with growth regulated and soil moisture held through targeted, approved treatments, so the surface is healthy, uniform and fit for every event. Treatments are applied only when needed under an integrated pest management approach, at the right time, evenly and at label rates, with no turf damage, no off-target contamination and the least risk to people and the environment.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4). Includes monitoring and inspection for turf pests, diseases, earthworm activity and weeds; preventative and curative control treatments; plant growth regulators; wetting agents; product procurement, storage and records; spray notification, signage and the treatment log. Fertiliser and nutrition products are covered in Section 6.
LoS 1 Pitch, event weeks (Premier). LoS 2 Pitch, training, non-event, renovation and grow-in weeks. LoS 3 Run-off and warm-up zones. LoS 4 Grass surrounds inside the perimeter.

Turf and soil profile inspected weekly for pest, disease, earthworm and weed activity at fixed monitoring plots and across the full surface. Action thresholds for each pest, disease and weed set in the Turf Management Plan; treatment triggered before significant turf damage occurs.
Integrated pest management monitoring log with plot records, counts and photographs; laboratory diagnosis where the cause is uncertain.
KPI-T monthly deduction if damage occurs without a timely response

No active disease scars or pest damage visible in Z1 to Z3 at readiness sign-off. Any outbreak contained and treated within 48 hours of detection. Fungicide use minimised and active ingredient groups rotated to manage resistance.
LoS 1 to 3; every event and continuous
Visual audit against Schedule 3 photo standards; outbreak register with detection and treatment dates; treatment log showing product rotation.
Joint readiness walk; Principal's agronomist monthly
No earthworm casts visible on the field of play at readiness sign-off; casts dispersed before mowing; control products timed with rainfall or irrigation as the label requires.
Visual audit of the field of play; cast counts at monitoring plots; treatment log.
Supplier before every event; joint readiness walk
Weeds controlled before they compromise the appearance, integrity or performance of the surface; targeted weeds fully controlled; weed cover in the field of play no more than 1%.
Weed cover assessment at monitoring plots; visual audit; treatment log.
Principal's agronomist monthly; Supplier weekly inspection
KPI-T monthly deduction if breached at audit

Applied only with the Principal's Representative's approval and to the approved programme. Growth regulators coordinated with the mowing plan (M1.3) and event peaking (N1.6), with no regulator discolouration at events. Wetting agents keep wetting uniform with no localised dry patch (I1.3).
Programme against application log; growing degree day or interval record; dry patch and colour assessment at monitoring plots.
KPI-T monthly deduction if breached at audit

Approved products applied evenly to the full extent at label rates and water volumes with calibrated equipment, using wetting, sticking and anti-drift agents as the label requires. No application where wind, rain, heat or soil moisture would compromise efficacy or uniformity; irrigation applied after application where the label requires.
Calibration record for each sprayer and spreader; treatment log with product, rate, water volume, weather and area; product reconciliation.
Supplier every application; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-T monthly deduction per confirmed incident

Agrichemicals applied only by GROWSAFE certified operators in line with NZS 8409 and TAU policy. Spray notification given to the Principal's Representative at least one week before work and recorded in the Spray Notification Register. Signs at all entry points until application is complete. Re-entry no longer than 'when fully dry'; residual products only with approval.
Applicator certificates; Spray Notification Register; signage photographs; product labels and safety data sheets on file.
Supplier every application; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-T monthly deduction per confirmed incident

No phytotoxicity, scorch or turf damage from products or application method; no pollution of drains, watercourses or water supply. Any incident reported immediately; damage repaired at the Supplier's cost.
Visual audit; monthly agronomic condition audit; incident register; Supplier early-warning notice.
KPI-T monthly deduction per confirmed incident
No treatment applied within 48 hours of kick-off unless agreed with the stadium turf manager; re-entry period ended and no residue or odour on the surface before bump-in and team walk-throughs.
Treatment log against the event run sheet; joint readiness walk.

Products ordered and delivered in time for the programme; stored safely and to legislative requirements; turf-registered products used where available; no exclusive supply arrangement without approval. Treatment log complete (location, product, rate, quantity, timing, applicator) and reconciled with claims.
Monthly treatment report; inventory reconciliation; treatment log provided on request.
KPI-T monthly deduction if late or incomplete

subs.title: Treatment programme guidelines (referenced by T1.1 to T1.5 and T1.9)

rows.t: Monitor first, set action thresholds, use cultural controls (clipping removal, irrigation and nutrition management, airflow and drainage) before chemical controls, and choose the most targeted product when treatment is needed.
Monitor for grass grub, black beetle, porina and Argentine stem weevil with soil cores and larval counts; treat at the threshold, timed to the susceptible life stage.

Monitor for Microdochium (fusarium) patch, dollar spot, red thread, anthracnose and leaf spot; use weather-based risk periods to time preventative applications; rotate active ingredient groups and keep fungicide use to the minimum needed.

Cultural control first (clipping removal, acidifying nitrogen carriers such as ammonium sulphate, Section 6); control products timed before rainfall or irrigation as the label requires; casts dispersed before mowing.
Spot treatment preferred; selective products chosen for the turf species; no residual products before seeding or turfing (R1.6).
Rate and re-application interval set by a growing degree day model or the approved interval; coordinated with the mowing plan and event peaking so turf is not discoloured or slowed in recovery.
Programme through the warm season to keep wetting uniform and reduce water use; product type matched to need (penetrant or retention) and coordinated with irrigation.
No treatment within 48 hours of kick-off unless agreed; re-entry period ended and surface clear before bump-in; curative treatment of an outbreak agreed with the stadium turf manager.

blocks.t: Standards T1.1 to T1.10 feed KPI-T, Turf Health and Treatments. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here.
The number of treatments does not enter KPI-T; curative treatments are reconciled annually against the declared treatment band (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for sports turf maintenance treatments:
The integrated pest management approach, monitoring plots and frequency, and action thresholds for each pest, disease and weed
The preventative programme and the curative response for each pest and disease, including active ingredient rotation
The earthworm management approach
The growth regulator programme and how it is coordinated with mowing and event peaking
The wetting agent programme and how it is coordinated with irrigation
Product selection, procurement, storage and the approved product list
Application equipment, calibration and weather decision rules
Spray notification, signage and public safety management
Event-week treatment rules
Applicator certification, resourcing and cover for absence
The treatment programme and every product are approved by the Principal's Representative before application.
Agrichemicals are handled and applied in line with current legislation, TAU policy and plans, the manufacturer's label and NZS 8409, by GROWSAFE certified operators.
Growth regulators and wetting agents are applied only with the Principal's Representative's approval.
No agrichemical with a re-entry period longer than 'when fully dry' is used, and residual products are used only with approval.
Spray notification is given at least one week ahead, and signs are placed at all entry points until application is complete.
Any pollution of a drain, watercourse or water supply is reported to the Principal's Representative immediately.
Operators have appropriate safety equipment; products are stored to the manufacturer's requirements and the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017.
Any turf damage from products or application is repaired at the Supplier's cost.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code and kick-off time 10 working days before commencement; approves the treatment programme and products within 10 working days of submission; supplies TAU-procured products on time where TAU elects to procure; has its agronomist review monitoring records and the monthly report; and attends the joint readiness sign-off.
Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-T for that event is assessed against what could be delivered in the revised window.

Monitoring, preventative treatments, application labour and reporting are priced as an annual lump sum per level of service, with a declared minimum and maximum number of curative treatments (the treatment band). Products are either supplied by TAU or supplied by the Supplier at the tendered rates in the Schedule of Rates. Curative treatments beyond the band are priced from the Schedule of Rates and approved in advance by the Principal's Representative.
The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Sports turf physical treatments (aeration, slicing and spiking, verti-draining, needle tining, hybrid turf grooming and rolling)
Schedule 2, Sports Turf Physical Treatments; standards feed KPI-P, Surface Condition and Playability, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The root zone is kept open, free draining and well rooted, and the surface firm, true and even, through physical treatments timed around the event calendar, so the pitch drains, recovers and plays consistently. Treatments are set up to suit the root zone and any hybrid system, leave the surface flat and playable, and cause no damage to the turf, the sand profile, hybrid fibres or buried assets.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4). The field of play includes stitched fibre and mat-backed hybrid zones, shown on the hybrid zone plan, and each treatment is matched to the zone. Includes solid tine and needle tine aeration (verti-drain), slicing and spiking, hybrid turf grooming, rolling, sand carpet depth checks, marking of irrigation, drainage and in-ground sensor assets before treatment, and surface testing to guide the programme. Deep decompaction and coring during renovation are covered by the renovation programme.
LoS 1 Pitch, event weeks (Premier). LoS 2 Pitch, training, non-event, renovation and grow-in weeks. LoS 3 Run-off and warm-up zones. LoS 4 Grass surrounds inside the perimeter.

Treatments delivered to the approved programme and timed around the event calendar: solid tine aeration not within 7 days before kick-off, needle tining not within 3 days, and slicing or spiking completed after rolling.
LoS 1 to 3; every event and monthly
Maintenance log of treatments against the approved programme and the event calendar.
Supplier monthly report; Principal's Representative review
Plant configured as approved (tine type, spacing, diameter, depth, heave) and the full extent of the surface treated.
Set-up record with photographs of tine configuration; GPS track or pass map; maintenance log.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction if breached at audit
No treatment when soil moisture would cause wheel marks, smearing, compaction, lasting heave, turf burial or other loss of surface quality.
Soil moisture reading before work (I1.2 probe); visual audit after treatment; photographs.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction per confirmed incident
Irrigation heads, valve boxes, drainage, in-ground moisture sensors and goal post sockets located and marked before work, with no damage to any of them.
Asset marking check before work; damage register.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction per confirmed incident
Sand carpet depth measured before work and penetration set shallower than the carpet, with no contamination or damage to the sand carpet, sand slits or sand bands.
Sand carpet depth readings and set depth recorded; profile check with a soil corer after treatment.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's agronomist spot check
KPI-P monthly deduction per confirmed incident

In natural turf zones: holes on a grid no larger than 150 x 150 mm, targeting at least 150 mm depth (shallower than any sand carpet). Heave targeted at 0% and never more than 5%, and used only with approval. Rear roller reinstates a flat surface; set deeper than the rooting depth where roots are weak or shallow.
Grid and depth measured at sample points; heave setting recorded; straightedge check after treatment.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction if breached at audit

Only solid or needle tines approved by the stitched system manufacturer, 12 mm diameter or less unless the manufacturer approves larger (proposed), set to a depth within the manufacturer's limit. Zero heave. No hollow coring, slicing blades or blade-type decompaction unless the manufacturer approves them. No fibres pulled out, cut or flattened.
Tine type and set-up record against the manufacturer's approval; fibre check at fixed grid points before and after; photographs.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction per confirmed incident

Needle tines or slim solid tines that pass cleanly through the mat, no larger than the mat system manufacturer's limit (8 mm proposed where no limit is stated), at the depth and hole density the manufacturer specifies. Zero heave. No hollow coring, slicing blades, blade-type decompaction (for example vibrating or ground-breaking blades) or any tool that can tear, lift or expose the mat.
Tine type and set-up record against the manufacturer's approval; mat inspection at sample points; arisings and surface checked for mat fragments; photographs.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction per confirmed incident

Spring tine rake, uni-rake or harrow at the start of the week after rolling, two passes as standard, to keep fibres upright and organic matter open. After every topdressing, fibres brushed or raked upright. At least 90% of fibres visible at monthly checks (proposed), and fibre exposure held at each manufacturer's specification. No damage to fibres or mat.
LoS 1 to 3; every treatment and monthly
Fibre visibility count at fixed grid points in each zone; fibre exposure measured; photographs.
KPI-P monthly deduction if breached at audit

Natural turf zones: tine spacing no more than 150 mm; depth at least 100 mm in soil profiles and shallower than the sand carpet in sand profiles; cavity at least 75 mm deep and no more than 10 mm wide. Stitched zones: only with equipment approved by the manufacturer. Mat-backed zones: not used.
Spacing, depth and cavity measured at sample points; zone checked against the hybrid zone plan; maintenance log.
KPI-P monthly deduction if breached at audit

Rolling after mowing, only when surface moisture allows tractor equipment without damage, using a Cambridge roller (flat roller only with approval), and balanced against compaction risk. A flat surface reinstated with no compaction, smearing or turf burial.
Rolling log against mowing log; straightedge check; visual audit.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-P monthly deduction if breached at audit

Surface firmness and evenness within the bands set in the Turf Management Plan for each code and each zone type, infiltration rate at or above the target for the root zone, and no surface disruption from treatments at readiness sign-off.
Clegg hammer or approved firmness readings on the 15-point grid; infiltration test at monitoring plots in each zone type; straightedge evenness checks.
Supplier monthly; Principal's agronomist; joint readiness walk

subs.title: Physical treatment guidelines (referenced by P1.1 and P1.6 to P1.11)

rows.t: Every treatment starts by confirming from the hybrid zone plan whether the area is natural turf, stitched hybrid or mat-backed hybrid. Where zones meet or overlap, the more restrictive set-up applies.

Grid no larger than 150 x 150 mm; at least 150 mm deep and shallower than the sand carpet; heave 0% target, 5% maximum, only with approval; rear roller set to leave a flat surface. Not within 7 days before kick-off.

Solid or needle tines approved by the stitched system manufacturer (12 mm diameter or less unless approved, proposed), to the manufacturer's depth limit; zero heave; no hollow coring, slicing blades or blade decompaction without the manufacturer's approval. Needle tining not within 3 days before kick-off; solid tining not within 7 days.

Needle or slim solid tines that pass cleanly through the mat (8 mm proposed where the manufacturer states no limit), at the manufacturer's depth and hole density; zero heave; no hollow coring, slicing blades, blade-type decompaction or any tool that can tear, lift or expose the mat. Not within 3 days before kick-off.

Natural turf zones: tine spacing no more than 150 mm; at least 100 mm deep in soil and shallower than the sand carpet in sand; cavity at least 75 mm deep and no more than 10 mm wide; after rolling. Stitched zones: manufacturer-approved equipment only. Mat-backed zones: not used.

Spring tine rake, uni-rake or harrow at the start of the week after rolling; two passes as standard, more where organic matter builds up; fibres brushed upright after every topdressing; at least 90% of fibres visible (proposed).
After mowing, only when the surface is dry enough; Cambridge roller, flat roller only with approval; used to restore a flat surface after wet-weather use, balanced against compaction.
Confirm the zone type; mark irrigation, drainage, in-ground sensor and goal post socket assets; measure sand carpet depth; check soil moisture; check tines against the approved set-up for the zone.
Straightedge check for a flat surface; fibre and mat check in hybrid zones; record zone, set-up, depth and area in the maintenance log; firmness reading where the treatment affects playability.
Deep decompaction, coring and topdressing programmes are planned with the renovation programme (Section 10) and follow the same zone rules.

blocks.t: Standards P1.1 to P1.12 feed KPI-P, Surface Condition and Playability. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here.
The number of passes does not enter KPI-P; treatment passes are reconciled annually against the declared treatment band (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for sports turf physical treatments:
The annual physical treatment programme by zone and month, keyed to the event calendar
Plant and equipment for each treatment and the approved set-up (tines, spacing, diameter, depth, heave)
How sand carpet depth is measured and penetration depth set

The hybrid zone plan and the approved tines, depths and equipment for natural turf, stitched and mat-backed zones, with each manufacturer's approval; grooming method and how fibre exposure and mat condition are checked
Rolling method, equipment and decision rules
Soil moisture and weather decision rules for starting work
Asset location and marking before treatment
Surface testing (firmness, evenness, infiltration) and how results change the programme
Event-week windows for each treatment
Resourcing and cover for absence
Plant and equipment set-up is approved by the Principal's Representative before use; heave is used only with approval.
Irrigation, drainage, in-ground sensor and goal post socket assets are located and marked before work starts.
Penetration depth is always shallower than the sand carpet, and sand slits and bands are not damaged.

In hybrid zones only tines and equipment approved by each system manufacturer are used; hollow coring, slicing blades, heave and blade-type decompaction are not used in mat-backed zones, and in stitched zones only with the manufacturer's approval.
No treatment is carried out when ground conditions would damage the surface.
A flat roller is used only with the Principal's Representative's approval.
Any damage to turf, the sand profile, hybrid fibres or buried assets is repaired at the Supplier's cost.
All plant complies with health and safety law and the stadium site rules; operators are trained and inducted.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's code and kick-off time 10 working days before commencement; gives access in the agreed treatment windows; approves plant set-up and the annual programme; provides as-built drawings of the root zone, sand carpet, drainage and hybrid systems, the hybrid zone plan and each manufacturer's maintenance manual and warranty conditions; and attends the joint readiness sign-off.
Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-P for that event is assessed against what could be delivered in the revised window.

Physical treatments are priced as an annual lump sum per level of service, with a declared minimum and maximum number of treatment passes for each treatment type (the treatment band). Passes beyond the band are priced from the Schedule of Rates and approved in advance by the Principal's Representative.
The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Sports turf renovation (coring and compaction relief, soil recycling, scarification, surface removal of natural and hybrid turf, seeding, stolonising and topdressing)
Schedule 2, Renovations; standards feed KPI-V, Renovation and Recovery, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

Each renovation restores the playing surface by removing excess organic matter and contaminated surface layers, relieving compaction, re-establishing levels and drainage, and renewing dense, healthy turf cover, so the pitch is handed back event-ready within the renovation window. Renovations are planned from field assessment, matched to the root zone and any hybrid system, delivered to the approved programme with approved materials, and leave no damage to the sand profile, hybrid fibres or buried assets.

Playing surface including in-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z3) and grass surrounds inside the perimeter fence (Z4), including the hybrid turf system, which combines stitched fibre and mat-backed zones. Includes the annual renovation programme and reporting; coring and hollow tine aeration; compaction relief; soil recycling; scarification; natural turf and hybrid turf surface removal (top planing and fraise mowing); seeding and stolonising; topdressing; renovation materials (sand, soil, seed) supply, testing, delivery and storage; grow-in; and clean-up. Minor repairs are covered in Section 7 and routine physical treatments in Section 9.
LoS 1 Pitch, field of play (Z1). LoS 2 In-goal, run-off and warm-up zones (Z2 and Z3). LoS 3 Grass surrounds inside the perimeter (Z4). LoS 4 Renovation materials, stockpile and storage areas.

Annual programme based on field performance, soil profile and turf assessments and any independent condition assessment, customised to the code and level of play, and fitted to the renovation window in the event calendar. Includes turf species, current conditions, recommendations and rationale, treatment schedule, materials schedule, timing, subcontractors and costs. Approved by the Principal's Representative before 1 August each year. Costed renovation recommendations for the next financial year submitted before 30 September for TAU's operating budget.
Renovation programme document with photographs of current condition; approval record.
KPI-V monthly deduction if late or incomplete

Weekly renovation update by 3 pm Friday showing planned, completed, deferred and upcoming works with rationale; completion report for each treatment with date, issues, cumulative completion against programme and claim against budget; before and after photographs; included in the monthly contract report.
Weekly update reports; completion reports; photographs.
KPI-V monthly deduction if late or incomplete

Irrigation, drainage, in-ground moisture sensors and goal post sockets located and clearly marked on the ground before work. Plant type and configuration approved; runs planned to maximise run length and minimise turning; full extent of the specified area treated.
Asset marking check before work; set-up record; GPS track or pass map.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-V monthly deduction per confirmed incident

Work only when the soil is dry enough to avoid smearing or compaction. No lasting heave, wheel marking, turf burial or damage to surface levels. Treatment depth never exceeds the sand carpet, with no contamination of the sand carpet and no damage to sand slits or bands.
Soil moisture reading before work; sand carpet depth readings; profile cores after treatment; straightedge check.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's agronomist spot check
KPI-V monthly deduction per confirmed incident

Core holes round, not oval, at the target depth (at least 75 mm, never beyond the sand carpet) on a 50 x 50 mm grid (hollow tine verti-drain 150 x 150 mm) unless otherwise approved. Cores removed off-site within 24 hours, or shattered at the right moisture and worked in with a drag mat without layering. Compaction relief set to maximise rooting depth without surface heave; at least one pass. In hybrid zones, coring and compaction relief only as each system manufacturer permits; no hollow coring or blade-type decompaction in mat-backed zones.
Grid, depth and hole quality measured at sample points; core removal record; visual check for layering.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-V monthly deduction if breached at audit

Natural turf: mown first, surface dry, at least two passes in different directions, blades set to just touch the soil or sand, arisings collected after each pass and removed off-site, irrigation after, and sand carpets topdressed (target 5 mm) within one week. Hybrid turf: blades set for each system to its manufacturer's guidance, just touching the mat in mat-backed zones and at a depth that does not cut or pull fibres in stitched zones, with fibres brushed upright before topdressing.
Set-up and pass record; arisings disposal dockets; visual check of fibres and surface; photographs.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-V monthly deduction if breached at audit

Removal to the approved depth with an even cut, no overlaps and no missed strips; missed areas and areas around irrigation heads removed to the same depth by approved methods; all material collected at the time of removal and taken off-site. Timed so the turf is actively growing with enough recovery time before dormancy (warm-season grasses), and followed by compaction relief and topdressing as required (Surface removal guidelines, 10.4.1).
Depth checks on a grid across each pass; disposal dockets; photographs; follow-up treatment records.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-V event score for the first event after renovation

The pitch combines stitched fibre and mat-backed hybrid systems. Removal depth is set zone by zone from a pre-works survey of fibre height, organic layer depth and depth to the mat, so cutting tools never contact the mat in mat-backed zones and never cut or pull out fibres in stitched zones; where the systems meet or overlap the shallower limit applies. Method agreed with each system manufacturer where the warranty requires it. Pitch then aerated, seeded and topdressed, with fibres standing upright and fibre exposure and infill restored to each manufacturer's specification (Surface removal guidelines, 10.4.2).
Pre-works and post-works survey at fixed grid points in each system zone; check of arisings for fibre and mat fragments; photographs; manufacturer sign-off where required.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative and hybrid system manufacturer where required
KPI-V event score for the first event after renovation

Approved species, cultivar and rate; seeding in at least two directions after scarification and before topdressing; irrigation within 12 hours and through establishment (at least 14 days). Stolons from an approved donor site, spread at target density within one working day of harvest, incorporated and covered by topdressing, with no water stress.
Seeding and stolonising records with species, rate, directions and times; irrigation log; establishment photographs.
KPI-V monthly deduction if breached at audit

Approved material applied evenly to the approved depth in passes in different directions, worked in by brush, drag mat or broom, with all hollows filled and no turf burial. The surface is not water stressed before topdressing starts.
Material approval record; depth checks; straightedge check; visual audit.
Supplier every treatment; Principal's Representative at audits
KPI-V monthly deduction if breached at audit

Sand, soil and seed meet the Renovation materials specification (10.5), with test certificates provided before delivery; non-conforming material removed at the Supplier's cost. Delivery, stockpiling and storage meet the specification, with drainage channels and outlets protected.
Sand batch test certificates and retained samples; soil test results where requested; seed analysis certificates; delivery dockets; stockpile inspection.
Supplier every delivery; Principal's Representative approval before use
KPI-V monthly deduction per non-conforming delivery

Grow-in monitored for six weeks; pitch handed back by the agreed date with turf cover, density, firmness and evenness within the handover criteria in the Turf Management Plan. Storage and access areas swept or blown clean within 24 hours (48 hours where several sites are renovated in succession), with no material in sumps, drains or channels.
Grow-in log with photographs; handover inspection with cover, firmness and evenness readings; clean-up inspection.
Supplier; joint handover inspection with the Principal's Representative
KPI-V event score for the first event after renovation

subs.title: Renovation treatment guidelines (referenced by V1.5, V1.6, V1.9 and V1.10)

rows.t: Tine spacing and diameter set for round core holes at the target depth (at least 75 mm, never beyond the sand carpet); 50 x 50 mm grid, or 150 x 150 mm for hollow tine verti-drain. In hard soils use shorter tines or shallower depth after rain or irrigation. At least one pass; passes and depth agreed on site. Hybrid zones: only as each manufacturer permits; not in mat-backed zones.

Cores collected and removed off-site within 24 hours, or left to dry to the right moisture, shattered by rotary mower or approved plant and worked in with a drag mat to fill low areas without layering. Cores may be moved to another approved site with approval.

Blade type, spacing and depth set to maximise compaction relief and rooting depth without heave; blades, knives and bullets not worn; direction set to intercept existing drainage. At least one pass. Not used in mat-backed hybrid zones; in stitched zones only with the manufacturer's approval.

Approved recycling dresser set field by field to minimise heave and turf damage while relieving compaction; enough material brought up to smooth levels without smothering turf; integrated stone sieve; at least 70 mm deep; field mown and scarified first; combined with overseeding where applicable.

Intensity matched to organic matter build-up and turf health; mown first, dry surface; at least two passes in different directions with blades just touching the soil or sand; arisings collected after each pass (single pass scarify and collect preferred); irrigation after; sand carpets topdressed to 5 mm within one week.

Approved equipment set for each system: blades just touching the mat in mat-backed zones, and set so fibres are not cut or pulled in stitched zones; arisings collected and removed; flexible drag mat to expose fibres, then brushing or raking to stand fibres up before topdressing.

Method suited to area and condition (dimple seeding, under-sowing, broadcasting or a combination); approved species, cultivar and rate; at least two directions with seed split evenly; small seed bulked with a carrier; after scarification and before topdressing (maximum 5 mm cover); irrigation within 12 hours and for at least 14 days.

Approved, prepared donor site; short stolons with multiple growth points spread evenly at target density within one working day of harvest; incorporated with a Cambridge roller and covered by sand topdressing; irrigated straight after; sequenced across the field in warm weather; grow-in monitored for six weeks.

Approved material inspected before use; applied evenly in passes in different directions to the approved depth; worked in by brush, drag mat or 3-point linkage broom; hollows filled with no turf burial; surface not water stressed before work.

Hard surfaces, storage and loading areas swept or blown clean within 24 hours (48 hours for successive sites); no vegetative material on adjacent turf, assets, sumps, drains or channels; sumps and cesspits protected where material is stored on hard surfaces; signage if clean-up is delayed.

subs.title: Surface removal (referenced by V1.7 and V1.8)

blocks.t: Surface removal (top planing and fraise mowing) removes accumulated organic matter, contaminated surface layers or over-sown grasses and resets the surface. The approach differs for natural turf and hybrid turf, as set out below. Depth is always confirmed on site with the Principal's Representative.

rows.t: Top planing for deeper surface removal where organic matter, contamination or levels require a reset. Fraise mowing for shallower, aggressive removal of thatch and surface compaction where top planing is not practicable because of its longer recovery time, and when transitioning from over-sown cool-season grasses to warm-season grass.

Set on site from organic matter depth, grass type, surface levels and the renovation window, in consultation with the Principal's Representative; fraise depth balances removal of the organic layer with retaining enough turf for rapid recovery. Never deep enough to compromise the sand carpet.

Top planer discharging removed material directly into a high-sided vehicle; universal head or equivalent for fraise mowing; set for an even cut depth with no overlapping passes and no missed strips between passes.
Irrigation heads, valve boxes, in-ground moisture sensors and goal post sockets marked before work; missed strips and areas around assets removed to the same depth by hand or loader.
Warm-season grasses actively growing at the start, with enough recovery time before winter dormancy; scheduled inside the renovation window agreed in the event calendar.
All organic and vegetative material collected at the time of removal and taken off-site to an approved location; no stockpiles left on site.
Compaction relief to restore soil structure and drainage, topdressing to reinstate a smooth, true surface, and seeding or stolonising where needed; irrigation and six-week grow-in monitoring.

The pitch combines a stitched fibre system and a mat-backed system. The hybrid zone plan shows where each is installed and where they meet or overlap. Each zone is renovated to its own manufacturer's renovation guidance and warranty conditions, with the method agreed with each manufacturer before work where the warranty requires it.

In every zone, measure organic layer depth and fibre height above the surface at fixed grid points. In stitched zones also record fibre density and anchoring condition; in mat-backed zones measure depth from the surface to the top of the mat. Record fibre condition and take photographs.

Set zone by zone from the survey. Mat-backed zones: cutting tools never contact or expose the mat. Stitched zones: depth limited so fibres are not cut or pulled out. Where the systems meet or overlap, the shallower of the two limits applies. Equipment configured for hybrid surfaces so organic material is removed from between the fibres.

No fibre cutting, pull-out or flattening, and no tearing, lifting or exposure of the mat; arisings checked during work for fibre and mat fragments, with work stopped and set-up adjusted if any are found.
All arisings collected at the time of removal and taken off-site to an approved location.

Drag mat and brush to stand fibres upright; needle tine aeration; seeding in at least two directions; sand topdressing matched to the existing root zone to restore the infill level and fibre exposure specified for each system, including the specified sand depth over the mat in mat-backed zones; irrigation within 12 hours.
Post-works survey at the same grid points in each system zone; before and after photographs; depth records; sign-off from each manufacturer where the warranty requires it.

subs.title: Renovation materials specification (referenced by V1.10 and V1.11)

rows.t: Clean, washed, free-draining silica sand of quartz origin; free of soil, shells, pumice, roots, seeds, weed propagules, metals, plastics and organic debris; from a single consistent source for the season; light to mid buff colour (iron-stained or dark sands only with approval); marine sands washed to residual EC below 0.3 dS/m; sub-angular to sub-rounded; free flowing.

Less than 0.5% calcium carbonate. Percent passing: 2.0 mm 100%; 1.0 mm 90 to 100%; 0.50 mm 35 to 90%; 0.25 mm 0 to 50%; 0.125 mm 0 to 2%; 0.063 mm 0 to 1%. Grading wholly within the medium-coarse band (0.50 to 1.0 mm) and matched to the existing profile where practicable. A wider grading for level correction only with approval.

Batch testing by an IANZ-accredited or equivalent laboratory at least one test per 500 tonnes or per delivery lot, whichever is more frequent, completed before the programme starts; certificates referencing supplier, stockpile and delivery date provided before delivery; 2 kg retained sample per batch held for 12 months.

Covered trucks; stockpiles on a clean sealed, geotextile-lined or approved turf pad, no higher than 3 m and worked from one face; grades and sources not mixed without approval; drainage protected before delivery; security fencing where requested; delivery docket with supplier, source, weights, times and vehicle for every load.

Stone-free loam or sandy loam (60 to 80% sand, 5 to 15% clay, silt below 25%) with good aggregate structure from stripped grassland or cultivated land; no subsoil, peat, reclaimed or industrial-site soil; screened to 12 mm; free of foreign material, herbicide residues, pests and pathogens; tested for contaminants including asbestos where requested.

Clean trucks; stockpiles no higher than 2 m on a clean, free-draining pad protected from ponding, erosion and traffic; not placed or moved above the plastic limit; sources not mixed without approval; drainage protected.

Certified species and cultivars adapted to Auckland conditions with proven sports field performance (drought tolerance, recovery, lower fertiliser need, disease resistance, wear tolerance); blends of at least three cultivars, with at least 65% A-List approved varieties where A-List seed is used.

Purity at least 98% and germination at least 90%, with an analysis certificate issued within 12 months of delivery; endophyte seed (where used) at least 70% viable and stored below 25 °C; imported seed compliant with the MPI Import Health Standard with biosecurity clearance.

blocks.t: Standards V1.1 to V1.12 feed KPI-V, Renovation and Recovery. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here.
Renovation quantities do not enter KPI-V; treatments and materials are reconciled against the approved programme and budget (Schedule 1, Part E).

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for renovations:
How the annual renovation programme is built from field assessment, surface testing and the event calendar renovation window
The named Renovation Manager and their qualifications, and how subcontractors are managed
Plant and equipment for each treatment and the proposed set-up
The natural turf surface removal method, depth-setting process and follow-up treatments
The hybrid turf surface removal method for the stitched and mat-backed zones, the pre-works and post-works survey, and liaison with both manufacturers
Seed species and cultivars, stolon donor sites and grow-in programme
Sand, soil and seed sources, testing and delivery arrangements
Asset location and protection, and ground condition decision rules
Handover criteria and how the pitch is brought back to event standard
Clean-up, environmental controls and reporting

The Supplier provides a suitably qualified Renovation Manager (National Certificate in Sports Turf Management Level 4 or equivalent) as a key person; any change requires the Principal's Representative's approval.
Specialised renovation tasks (such as surface removal) are subcontracted only with the Principal's Representative's approval, and the Renovation Manager stays responsible for quality and reporting.
The renovation programme, plant set-up, materials and grass species are approved by the Principal's Representative before work starts.
Treatment depth never exceeds the sand carpet, and the sand carpet, slits, bands and hybrid system are not damaged.
Hybrid turf renovation follows each hybrid system manufacturer's guidance and warranty conditions, zone by zone.
All arisings, cores and removed material are taken off-site to an approved facility unless approved otherwise.
No vegetative material or sand enters sumps, stormwater systems or open channels.
The Supplier does not enter an exclusive supply arrangement for renovation products without approval.
All plant complies with health and safety law and the stadium site rules; operators are trained and inducted.

The Principal sets the renovation window in the event calendar at least 12 months ahead; approves the renovation programme before 1 August and any later changes; supplies TAU-procured products on time where TAU elects to procure; provides as-built drawings of the root zone, sand carpet, drainage and both hybrid systems, and the hybrid zone plan and the warranty conditions for both hybrid systems; and attends the joint handover inspection.
Where an event is added inside the renovation window, KPI-V for the first event after renovation is assessed against what could be delivered in the revised window.

Renovation treatments are priced per treatment and per m2 from the tendered rates in the Schedule of Rates, with materials priced separately (labour, plant, materials and other costs shown separately in the programme). The approved annual programme sets the budget; cumulative claims are reported against it weekly. Surface removal of natural and hybrid turf is priced separately, including disposal.
The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Sports turf operations and management (key personnel, Turf Management Plan, event readiness and event-day operations, pitch use and closures, non-sporting events, early warning, response, reporting, quality, health and safety)
Schedule 2, Sports Turf Operations & Management; standards feed KPI-O, Operations and Management, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

The turf services are led, planned, coordinated and reported as one integrated operation, so every event is prepared, signed off and supported on the day, the pitch is protected from overuse, wet-weather damage and non-sporting events, issues are found and fixed before they affect use, and the Principal has timely, accurate information to manage the stadium. The Supplier works as a proactive partner with a no-surprises culture.

All zones (stadium zone plan Z1 to Z4) and every service area in Sections 1 to 10. Includes key personnel; the Turf Management Plan; event readiness sign-off and event-day turf operations; pitch use, training allocation and wear management; wet-weather and closure management; protection and recovery for non-sporting events and overlays; Eyes and Ears early warning; response maintenance; reporting; quality assurance; stakeholder liaison with codes, competitions and broadcasters; and health, safety and environmental management.

LoS 1 Event operations (readiness, match day and post-event). LoS 2 Routine operations and pitch use management. LoS 3 Non-sporting events, overlays and closures. LoS 4 Contract management, reporting and quality.

A Stadium Turf Operations Manager (National Certificate in Sports Turf Management Level 4 or equivalent, with stadium event experience) leads the services as the single point of contact, supported by the Irrigation Specialist (Section 3) and Renovation Manager (Section 10). Key people changed only with the Principal's Representative's approval; trained cover nominated for absences.
Key personnel register with qualifications and cover arrangements; approval records.

A single Turf Management Plan bringing together the Supplier plan requirements of Sections 1 to 10, submitted at least 20 working days before the contract starts and reviewed annually by 1 June; updated within 10 working days of any material change and approved before use.
Turf Management Plan with version control; approval record; change log.
KPI-O monthly deduction if late or incomplete

Joint readiness walk for every event, completed at least 4 hours before kick-off, using the readiness checklist for all service area standards (mowing, line marking, irrigation, goal posts, sports lighting, nutrition, repairs, treatments and physical treatments). Every fail rectified before kick-off or recorded with the reason and agreed action.
Signed readiness checklist with readings and photographs; rectification record.
Supplier and Principal's Representative jointly; match commissioner where present

Turf team on site from the readiness walk until the pitch is handed back after the event; pre-match and half-time divoting and repairs; pre-match or half-time watering only where allowed (I1.4); goal post, padding and net checks; liaison with the match commissioner and referee at pitch inspections; post-event damage map within 24 hours. For double headers, between-match turf works (divoting, repairs, goal post and padding checks, line touch-ups and any agreed code changeover) are completed and checked before the second kick-off.
Event-day log with staff on site and times; half-time actions; post-event damage map.

Training and warm-up allocations managed to the use limits in the Turf Management Plan; usage log kept for every session; high-wear areas (goalmouths, warm-up zones, centre) rotated or protected; recommendations to restrict use given before damage occurs.
Usage log against allocations and use limits; wear-area photographs; recommendations log.
KPI-O monthly deduction if breached at audit

A nominated lead (and trained alternate) manages closures. Ground condition assessed daily in the playing season; closure or restriction recommendation to the Principal's Representative by 9.00 am on the day; for national or international matches, or teams travelling from outside Auckland, a cancellation recommendation at least 24 hours before kick-off where extreme weather is forecast.
LoS 3; daily in season and every event
Closure Inspection Form; timestamped recommendations; weather forecast record.
KPI-O monthly deduction if late or inaccurate

Protection plan agreed before every non-sporting event or overlay (covers, ground protection, access routes, load limits); pre-event condition survey; covers in place no longer than the duration agreed in the protection plan; post-event condition survey and recovery plan within 48 hours of removal.
Protection plan; pre- and post-event condition surveys with photographs; recovery plan.
Supplier; joint inspection with the Principal's Representative
KPI-O monthly deduction if late or missed

All Supplier staff report issues seen on every visit (safety hazards, unauthorised use, access or gate damage, unlocked cabinets or controllers, irrigation faults or leaks, water-stressed or unhealthy turf, pests and disease, damaged equipment, vandalism, graffiti, dumping, stakeholder complaints). Logged the same day and notified to the Principal's Representative; safety issues immediately.
Early warning log with times and actions; evidence that issues were raised before any complaint.
KPI-O monthly deduction per issue missed or not reported

After-hours and weekend response register with escalation tree, updated weekly. Requests for service met within the RFS timeframes: Critical, response 1 hour and completion 2 hours; Priority 2, response 4 hours and completion 8 hours; Urgent, response 24 hours and completion 48 hours. Site made safe where not resolved at the first visit; response report with before and after photographs. A named on-call turf staff member is available for weekend and event-day sport and can be on site within 1 hour (proposed).
Response register; RFS records with response and completion times; response reports.
Supplier every request; Principal's Representative monthly
KPI-O monthly deduction per late response

Weekly report by 3.00 pm Friday (works completed and planned, event readiness, issues, closures, response register); monthly contract report with the evidence for every KPI, water, nutrition, treatment and renovation data; annual condition report. All reports accurate, complete and in the approved formats.
Reports received against due dates; accuracy checks against logs and audits.
KPI-O monthly deduction if late or inaccurate

Quality plan with monthly internal audits against the standards; non-conformance register with corrective actions closed within the agreed time; monthly performance meeting with the Principal's Representative; annual improvement plan agreed with the Principal.
Quality plan; internal audit records; non-conformance register; meeting minutes; improvement plan.

Site-specific safety plan aligned to the stadium site rules; all staff and subcontractors inducted; incidents reported to the Principal's Representative within 24 hours and notifiable events immediately; environmental controls in place for fuel, chemicals, wash-down and stormwater.
Safety plan; induction register; incident register; environmental inspection records.
KPI-O monthly deduction per confirmed breach

Requests from TAU's events team for event-day works (additional staff on site, extra preparation, reinstatement) acknowledged within 1 working day and quoted within 3 working days (proposed), showing staff numbers, hours, plant and rates; works delivered as quoted and invoiced against the approved quote.
Request and quote register with dates; approved quotes; invoices against quotes.
KPI-O monthly deduction per late quote

Turf protection flooring installed, cleaned and removed to the agreed protection plan (O1.7) and the flooring manufacturer's guidance; installed no earlier and removed no later than the agreed times; surface cleared of debris; turf condition surveyed before and after.
Flooring log with installation and removal times and area in m2; condition surveys; photographs.
Supplier; joint inspection with the Principal's Representative

subs.title: Event operations timeline (referenced by O1.3 and O1.4)

rows.t: Event calendar issued by the Principal; event preparation dates and renovation windows set in the Turf Management Plan programme.
Principal confirms code, competition, kick-off time, event tier, broadcast requirements, mowing pattern, marking drawing, padding and nets, and any watering requests.

Preparation programme delivered across all service areas (mowing, line marking, irrigation, nutrition peaking, repairs, treatments); daily condition checks; pitch use restricted to the agreed allocation.
Final cut and line marking; readiness pre-check by the Supplier; captain's run or team walk arrangements confirmed with the Principal.
Match day, at least 4 hours before kick-off
Joint readiness walk and sign-off against the readiness checklist; any fails rectified before kick-off.
Turf team on standby for divoting, repairs, goal post and padding checks, and watering where allowed.
Post-event damage map; divoting (R1.2); recovery feed (N1.7); post-event summary to the Principal.
Compressed timeline agreed with the Principal when events are less than 7 days apart.

Where two matches are played on the same day, the readiness sign-off covers both; between matches the turf team completes divoting, repairs, goal post and padding checks, line touch-ups and any code changeover agreed in the run sheet, within the window set by TAU.

subs.title: Reporting and response schedule (referenced by O1.6, O1.9 and O1.10)

rows.t: To the Principal's Representative by 9.00 am on the day; TAU communicates closures by 10.00 am weekdays and 7.00 am at weekends.
Recommendation at least 24 hours before kick-off for national or international matches, or teams travelling from outside Auckland, when extreme weather is forecast.
Logged the same day; safety issues reported immediately.
Updated weekly with after-hours and weekend contacts and the escalation tree.
Named on-call turf staff for weekend and event-day sport, on site within 1 hour (proposed); listed in the response register.
Critical: response 1 hour, completion 2 hours. Priority 2: response 4 hours, completion 8 hours. Urgent: response 24 hours, completion 48 hours.
Work under $1,000 that presents an immediate risk to safety or pitch use may proceed without approval; work over $1,000 requires the Principal's Representative's approval.
Requests from TAU's events team acknowledged within 1 working day and quoted within 3 working days (proposed).
By the fifth working day of the following month, with KPI evidence for every service area.
Costed condition reports and recommendations for irrigation, goal posts, sports lighting, renovation and compliance testing submitted before 30 September for TAU's operating budget.
Turf Management Plan review by 1 June; condition report and improvement plan with the annual contract review.

blocks.t: Standards O1.1 to O1.14 feed KPI-O, Operations and Management. Scoring, pass threshold and weighting are defined once in the Performance Model (Schedule 1, Parts B and C) and are not repeated here.
Event readiness results for each service area are scored in that service area's KPI; KPI-O scores how the readiness process, event-day operations and contract management are run.

subs.title: Supplier plan requirements (Turf Management Plan content)

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for operations and management:
The organisation structure, key personnel, qualifications and cover arrangements
How the Supplier plan requirements of Sections 1 to 10 are integrated into one annual programme keyed to the event calendar
The event readiness checklist and event-day operations plan
Pitch use limits, training allocation and wear management approach
Wet-weather assessment and closure decision process
The protection and recovery approach for non-sporting events and overlays
The Eyes and Ears early warning process and staff training
The response service, register and escalation tree
Reporting formats, systems and timetable
The quality plan, internal audit programme and improvement approach
The site-specific health, safety and environmental plan
The Stadium Turf Operations Manager, Irrigation Specialist and Renovation Manager are key persons; any change requires the Principal's Representative's approval.
No event proceeds without a completed joint readiness sign-off.
All Supplier staff take part in Eyes and Ears early warning on every visit.
The response register is kept current and staff are contactable as registered.
If the Supplier cannot be contacted or fails to attend an emergency call-out within the response time, TAU may engage another supplier and recover the cost from the Supplier.
All staff and subcontractors are inducted to the stadium site rules and comply with health and safety law.
The Supplier communicates with codes, competitions and broadcasters only as agreed with the Principal's Representative.

The Principal issues the event calendar at least 12 weeks ahead and confirms each event's details 10 working days before; sets training allocations and approves use limits; decides closures, cancellations and non-sporting uses and bears the recovery consequences under Schedule 1; communicates closures to users and the public; provides access to the booking, RFS and reporting systems; attends the joint readiness sign-off and monthly performance meeting; and approves the Turf Management Plan. TAU's events team requests event-day works and event flooring in writing with the event details at least 10 working days before the event (proposed).
Where the calendar changes inside the notice period, KPI-O for that event is assessed against what could be delivered in the revised window.

Operations management, key personnel, Turf Management Plan, reporting, quality and the response service are priced as an annual lump sum. Event-day attendance is priced per event with a declared minimum and maximum number of events (the event band). Response work is priced from the Schedule of Rates within the response cost thresholds. Recovery after non-sporting events is instructed and priced separately under Schedule 1. Event-day works requested by TAU's events team (additional staff on site, extra preparation or reinstatement) are quoted from the Schedule of Rates (hourly staff rates and plant rates). Event flooring is priced per m2 for installation, cleaning and removal.
The band operates as set out in Schedule 1, Part E.

rows.t: Field compliance testing (routine surface performance testing of training fields and #1 fields, the standard results format, and reporting to TAU)
Schedule 2, Field Compliance Testing; standards feed KPI-C, Surface Compliance, in Schedule 1, Performance Model

Every field's playing quality and safety is measured on a regular cycle with consistent methods, so TAU has objective evidence that each surface is within the performance bands for its codes, trends are seen early, and maintenance is adjusted before a surface falls out of compliance. Results are recorded in one agreed format and sent to TAU on time.

All #1 (match) fields and training fields in the asset schedule (Appendix B). Includes weekly testing of training fields and fortnightly testing of #1 fields during the playing season, pre-event testing for Tier A events, the standard test template, calibration of test equipment, data storage and reporting to TAU. Independent testing commissioned by TAU is not included.
LoS 1 #1 (match) fields. LoS 2 Training fields. LoS 3 Pre-event testing. LoS 4 Data, reporting and equipment.

Training fields tested every week and #1 fields every fortnight during the playing season, plus a test round within 48 hours before every Tier A event (proposed). Frequency outside the playing season agreed with TAU.
Test register against the testing schedule.
KPI-C monthly deduction per missed test round
Each test round records surface hardness, rotational traction, soil moisture, live grass cover, sward height and surface evenness, plus fibre visibility in hybrid zones; infiltration tested monthly.
Completed test template for each field.

Tests taken at fixed points on the zone plan for each field (the 15-point grid used for M1.1, plus goalmouth and other high-wear points), using the methods in the test template, with weather and surface conditions recorded.
Test point map; method statement; photographs of test points.
KPI-C monthly deduction if breached at audit
Results compared with the performance bands for each code set in the Turf Management Plan and approved by TAU, and rated green (within band), amber (approaching the limit) or red (outside band).
Rated results in the test template.

Amber results addressed in the next maintenance programme. Red results reported to TAU within 24 hours with a corrective action plan, and the field retested after the action. No event on a red result for a safety-related parameter (hardness, traction or evenness) without a TAU decision.
KPI-C monthly deduction per late or missed action
Test equipment calibrated to the manufacturer's requirements and at least annually, with calibration certificates held; operators trained in the test methods.

Results entered in the standard test template agreed with TAU and sent to TAU within 2 working days of each test round, stored in the agreed shared location; monthly summary with trends for each field; annual compliance report by 30 September to inform the next year's budget.
LoS 4; every test round, monthly and annual
Template submissions against due dates; monthly summaries; annual report.
KPI-C monthly deduction if late or incomplete
Raw readings kept for the term of the contract; results owned by TAU; any correction to submitted data logged with the reason.
KPI-C monthly deduction per confirmed breach

rows.t: Training fields every week; #1 fields every fortnight; within 48 hours before every Tier A event (proposed); infiltration monthly. Outside the playing season as agreed with TAU.
Clegg impact hammer (2.25 kg) or approved equivalent at every test point; method and drop sequence as set out in the test template.
Studded traction tester at every test point.
Approved moisture probe (e.g. POGO or TDR) at every test point, at the depths set in the template (including 40 mm for event moisture, I1.1).

Straightedge or approved evenness device along set lines; maximum deviation recorded.

blocks.t: The Turf Management Plan shall show for field compliance testing:
The testing schedule for each field in the asset schedule
Test methods, equipment and fixed test point maps for each field

Use of the pitch and surrounds is measured objectively and continuously, showing how many people use the surface, when, for how long and where, and is turned into usage hours and heat maps that drive maintenance decisions on wear, repairs, physical treatments, renovation and use limits. Cameras online and capturing during all event, training and booked use; data available for at least 95% of scheduled use hours each month (pilot); camera faults, obstructions or connectivity loss reported to the Principal's Representative within 24 hours.
Platform availability report; fault log; check of camera views before events.

Validation log with sample sessions, manual counts and variance.
Usage reported as usage hours, user hours (people multiplied by time), peak numbers and activity type (match, training, warm-up, maintenance, non-sporting), by zone of the stadium zone plan.
Monthly usage report and dashboard export.
